Better.

Different category.

No broken skin.

Simple.

"That's office property."

Thin.

Hip soreness less.

Good.

"Useful."

I looked at slate.

Three-day flex.

No minimum.

Could work.

Could fit.

Could leave.

Could labor board.

Could go auction and become poor idiot.

Could maybe travel farther.

Option.

Again.

"Yes," I said.

Tavren nodded.

Done.

No contract ceremony.

Good.

Then Nali said, "Masta said come by."

I looked at her.

"Today?"

"Skin check only. No shell unless she changes mind."

Good.

I went.

Hark & Venn smelled like warm leather and oil.

Masta looked at me.

"Pants."

"You really should vary greeting."

"No."

Skin check.

Upper redness gone.

Posterior line gone.

No abrasion.

She pressed around stump.

"Sore?"

"Hip. Not skin."

"Expected."

"Right calf too."

"Good."

"Means you actually loaded left side enough to change right-side pattern."

There.

Evidence.

Small.

Real.

She turned toward bench.

Trial shell sat there.

Adjusted.

I looked.

She caught look.

"No shell today."

"I know."

Everyone had face theory.

"Tomorrow?"

"If skin stays clean."

"Tomorrow after work?"

"After whatever you do. Come before sixth bell."

"How long?"

"Until I stop."

Good.

Then she did something rude.

She handed me shell.

Not to wear.

Just hold.

"Feel weight."

I took it.

Lighter than expected.

Not light.

Support post and test foot gave awkward balance.

Socket itself dense.

"Finished one heavier?"

"A little. Better foot. Side stay maybe. Hardware."

"How much heavier?"

"Enough you'll complain."

"Useful."

"You'll get used to some. Not all."

I turned shell in hands.

Object made for body.

Strange category.

Armor was made for body.

Weapons too.

Boots.

Braces.

But this was closer.

Not replacement.

Interface.

Masta took it back before I became philosophical.

Good woman.

"Tomorrow we walk again," she said.

"Better?"

"Maybe."

"How encouraging."

"I don't care if better. I care if data better."

Right.

Walk honestly.

I left.

Outside, dusk light across street.

I stood on crutches.

Familiar.

Fast.

Efficient.

No shame in that.

Important.

Future leg did not need to defeat crutches to justify itself.

It needed to add options.

I headed toward inn.

Halfway there, someone called my name.

Not Peg-Leg.

Greg.

Sori.

She was standing outside post office with folded paper.

My stomach changed before brain did.

Home.

She held it out.

"Carrow."

There.

Finally.

I took paper.

Cala's handwriting on outside.

Not elegant.

Fast.

I opened.

Three hands inside.

Cala first.

**You went farther than two nights. Obviously. Theatre still standing. Vale asked twice whether you're dead. I told him probably not. Work is work. Don't make us come get you because you decided sea is personality now.**

I laughed.

Then Tavi.

Big crooked letters.

**DID YOU SEE A SEA MONSTER. BRING ROCK IF SEA ROCK DIFFERENT. COME BACK BUT NOT YET IF YOU ARE DOING IMPORTANT THING.**

Chest hurt.

Small.

Good hurt.

Then Lyssa.

Neater.

**I am glad you went. I am also annoyed you went far enough that being glad takes effort. Both can be true. Cala says that is adulthood. Cala is wrong about many things but not this one. Send dates when you know them. Do not turn uncertainty into disappearance.**

Sori watched face.

"Bad?"

"No."

"Good?"

"Annoying."

"So good."

"Yes."

Come back but not yet.

Smart kid.

Dangerous.

Worse.

Send dates when you know them.

Tomorrow shell.

Three-day flex work.

Maybe a few more days Duskport.

Then?

Road had widened.

Could go back.

Could go farther.

Could wait until leg usable enough for travel trials.

Could not pretend no choice existed.

There.

Different pressure.

At Anchor's End I wrote reply before dinner.

Not long.

**Alive. Duskport. Working temporary harbor recovery. Paid deposit on work leg. First trial shell happened. Worse than crutches so far, which is apparently correct. Staying at least several more days for fittings and work. After that I don't know yet. I will send another date when I do. Sea monster: one chain ray, which probably counts. Tavi, sea rocks are different.**

I stopped.

Added:

**I miss you.**

There.

Simple.

No need to be clever.

Good.

Good friends.

Still Vale.

Still food.

Still room.

Not trapped.

Expected.

Different.

Fast.

Familiar.

# CHAPTER 423

## THE PATIENT

Morning skin looked boring.

Best possible result.

No heat.

No open spot.

No angry line.

Hip still sore if I leaned wrong.

Right calf less annoyed than yesterday.

Good.

I sent Carrow letter at first bell.

Actually watched courier pouch get tied.

Did not help.

Still felt better.

Communication apparently required ritual.

Sori stood beside me.

"You trust mail now?"

"No."

"Good."

"I trust knots."

"Worse."

We walked back toward East Hook.

I stopped halfway.

She stopped too.

"What?"

"I don't think I'm working today."

Sori looked at me.

Not surprised.

That annoyed me slightly.

"Why?"

"Second shell tonight."

"And?"

"Yesterday Masta said work normally. Today she didn't say work normally."

"She also didn't say don't."

"Correct."

"So?"

"I want clean legs."

"Plural?"

"Body."

"Better."

I hated language.

Thirty-nine copper.

Work available maybe.

Three-day flex.

No minimum.

Whole point.

Still.

Money sat in head.

Sori said, "You know not earning three or four copper today won't make leg disappear."

"Yes."

"Do you believe that?"

I looked at her.

"Less."

"Good enough."

East Hook anyway.

"Oh!"

"Bad."

There.

Small thing.

Stable enough standing.

Not Masta courtyard.

Street.

"I know."

"You look emotional."

"Fuck bread."

She laughed harder.

Walked.

Roll in bag.

One block.

Concentration expensive.

Every left placement required thought.

Right knee wanted old lock when crowd passed close.

Shoulders wanted lift.

Crutches wanted become primary again because they knew job.

I let them when needed.

That was part I had not expected emotionally.

Yesterday maybe would.

Today they were another tool.

Leg one tool.

Crutches another.

Switch based on problem.

At old fountain I sat.

Timer by bell tower maybe eighteen minutes since shop.

I loosened nothing.

Residual limb warm.

General warm.

No point heat.

No pain.

Good.

"Some."

"Not today."

"Later?"

Boy whispered, "Who deserves it?"

"Go away."

He grinned.

I stood.

Standing from low fountain harder than walking.

Needed crutches strongly.

Right leg did most rise.

Shell caught load late.

Mental note.

Not ready for low chairs without arms.

Inventory.

Market edge busier.

I shortened route slightly to avoid wet fish paving.

Masta said flat, not stupid.

At one shop door woman came out carrying crate.

I stepped aside.

Old crutch habit: swing body quickly, plant both, clear lane.

New shell: slower lateral move.

Caught with crutch.

No fall.

Heart jumped anyway.

There.

Not magic.

Sideways sucked.

"Not you."

Shallow.

Nali had been right.

I swore.

Test foot was rigid enough that downhill placement wanted slap.

Short step.

Right.

Left.

Fine.

Then uphill other side easier.

Good.

Thirty-five minutes.

Not cardio exactly.

Concentration plus unfamiliar muscles.

No rail.

Five.

Then six.

Old old me.

First-life twenty-something me definitely.

First-life fifty-nine me maybe not.

Nobody.

Good.

Not leg.

For maybe thirty seconds.

Just where going.

Bread Street.

Fountain.

Glass Lane.

Thirty seconds.

Tiny.

Huge.

That was first glimpse.

Not hands.

Not standing.

Not even steps.

Attention.

Crutches had become invisible years ago because skill made them background.

This thing was screaming foreground every second.

Until it wasn't.

Thirty seconds.

Potential.

Back at shop forty-eight minutes after leaving.

Masta looked at clock.

"Early."

"Pattern degrading."

"Where?"

"Left foot drifting outward after six unsupported steps. Sideways movement bad. Down curb cut worse than up. Low fountain stand needs crutches heavily. General warmth, no point heat."

"No."

"No."

No fake discount.

Of course.

No date.

Annoying.

Correct.

Fast.

Easy.

Familiar.

No contest.

Normally one crutch under arm, free hand door, awkward pivot.

Both hands.

Not yet.

Soon.

"Worse."

"Hop Greg."

"Stop."

"Greg."

"Acceptable."

"Of course."

Bad.

Slow.

Tiring.

Useful.

Different.

"With both hands."

Small.

She got it.

"Oh."

"Yeah."

World map.

Not locked-in reserve.

Earlier than that.

Before rank.

Before reputation.

Training brain.

There.

Quiet.

Then right ankle.

Thought about balance.

Hip.

Turns.

Load.

Magic.

"Good."

Of course.

There.

Road could become fitting data.

Not reason to go.

Useful if went.

People arguing about whether causeway was safe.

Again.

Again.

Twenty courtyard minutes.

Box left.

Eight steps.

Nine.

"Good."

Left hand empty.

Shop front to corner and back.

Dry stone.

Maybe ten minutes.

Not good.

Better.

I used crutches fully.

No heroics.

Back.

Shell off.

Skin.

Pink upper edge.

Outer-distal almost nothing.

Waited another ten.

Gone.

**ROAD TEST / GREG / LEFT BKA**

Morning wear: maximum thirty minutes first day.

Evening wear: maximum thirty minutes.

Not consecutive.

No loaded walking except ordinary light hand carry on flat stable surface.

No marsh edge.

No mud deeper than sole tread.

No wagon jumping.

No running.

No ladders.

No worksite wear unless Enna and Greg both agree surface is stable and wear window remains.

Crutches primary.

Skin check immediately after removal and twenty minutes later.

Persistent redness at twenty minutes means no second wear period.

Blister, open skin, numbness, rising pain, point heat: stop until Masta or qualified fitter.

Daily notes:

surface.

time.

pain.

heat.

redness.

pattern failure.

"I don't care."

"Cruel."

"You're taking it?"

"Trial."

Maro smiled.

"Rules?"

All of it.

"Maybe."

"That's good."

"That was almost joke."

"It was accurate forecast."

No Black Keel.

No strong beer.

Sori checked passenger chits.

Maro tied shell necklace tighter.

Dask packed mirror again after I removed it once as public service.

He found it.

Unfortunate.

**Leaving north before first bell. Greyfin Road, then North Reach. Three field days minimum. I have trial leg with me, not finished one. I am not walking marsh in it. Tell Tavi that specifically.**

Crutches beside bed.

Trial build wrapped at foot.

Sable Quay had been stop.

Two nights.

Three days.

Cute.

Not disappearing.

Moving.

Good.

Silence.

Not because question bad.

Because answer long.

"Meaning either road crown lowered, archived tie was recorded badly, quarry face itself changed, or some combination. But R-four face mark is intact, and archive sketch matches current notch geometry. So I place more confidence in actual road lowering here than at South Approach."

"Enough to recommend against unrestricted heavy freight until loaded response is observed. Not enough to call whole causeway failed."

There.

Smaller claim.

Painful enough.

"One."

"How heavy?"

"Class ten loaded."

"Different section."

"Still decision after all three sections."

Tera's jaw tightened.

Enna met her eyes.

"Yes."

Tera almost laughed.

Didn't.

First relay had test wagon staged north side.

Class eight verified on scale blocks.

No argument this time.

Tender put sounding plate near shoulder.

Enna assigned me fixed observation position on ridge side.

"Do not move to see better."

"Yes."

"If something happens, write after you're safe."

"Yes."

Jorren said, "Comforting."

Wagon approached walking pace.

Two horses.

Driver pale.

Front axle crossed first stone seam.

Nothing.

Rear.

Small vibration through road.

I felt through right crutch tip.

Not measurement.

Did not write yet.

At north crack, left rear wheel sank visible amount.

Less than South dip maybe.

Different surface.

Then sound.

Not timber knock.

Stone grind.

Short.

Deep.

Driver stopped without instruction.

Good driver.

Nobody breathed.

Enna raised hand.

"Hold."

Halen crouched near crack but did not cross chalk.

Crack had extended.

Not much.

Visible.

Maybe finger length beyond yesterday chalk.

Today pre-pass endpoint also marked.

Now new hairline ran past by roughly two fingers.

I wrote time.

Axle class.

Wheel position.

Sound.

Stop.

Visible crack extension beyond pre-pass chalk approximately two fingers.

No cause.

No safe.

No failed.

"Fuck."

Not victory.

Important.

Halen stood.

Enna repeated to driver.

Wagon moved.

Then clear.

Halen inspected.

He took longer than anyone wanted.

Jorren stopped pacing.

Tera sat on stone.

I kept ledger open.

North Reach smoke ahead.

Fuel south.

Road between.

"Heavy freight hold remains."

"I would not repeat class eight here until shoulder is opened and inspected."

"Class six local?"

Halen looked at Enna.

Policy.

Enna looked at road, then Tera.

"Single class-six local carts. Walking pace. One at a time. No passing on Section Three. Spotter present until inspection."

Jorren asked, "Clinic drums can be broken to class six carts."

He shrugged.

"They can. Fuel convoy can't economically, but clinic drums can."

"Two carts maybe three depending drums."

"Guild charge?"

There.

Jorren's face changed.

Business.

"Normal transfer plus local haul."

Tera stood.

"No."

"I'm not donating team."

"Fuel rate assumes convoy delivery. Breaking load costs labor and delay."

"Road problem isn't ours."

"Correct."

"Still convenient."

"Yes."

That one hurt.

Correct procedure.

No clean answer.

Tera waited.

"Free?"

He looked physically ill.

"Yes."

Tera nodded once.

"I can find second."

Not compromise solved everything.

Enna wrote temporary traffic order.

**SECTION THREE HEAVY HOLD CONTINUES. CLASS SIX LOCAL SINGLE-PASS UNDER SPOTTER. NO REPEAT CLASS EIGHT PENDING SHOULDER INSPECTION.**

Authority: Enna Ro field lead on Halen Brusk survey recommendation.

Names mattered.

Who decided mattered.

My handwriting did not make it mine.

First relay stayed to spot traffic.

We moved north.

Not town exactly.

Depot with town growing around it.

Fuel sheds.

Repair yard.

Two inns.

Marsh on three sides and ridge road continuing north-east.

Beyond depot, signpost.

**MEREHOOK 2 DAYS**

**UPLAND FORK 3 DAYS**

I looked too long.

Enna said, "Don't plan past the contract yet."

"I wasn't."

"You looked too long."

"That proves nothing."

"Good."

Interesting.

Companions had passenger lodging at Reed Lamp across lane, included only through tonight in their fare.

"How bad?"

"More bad."

"Technical."

"Class eight extended crack at north shoulder. Heavy hold. Local six still moving one at time."

"Fuel?"

"Stopped south. Clinic drums getting broken out."

"Who pays?"

"Everyone arguing."

"So normal."

"Basically."

"Yes."

"Then guild was right."

"About benchmark."

"Both?"

"Apparently world supports multiple annoying truths."

Dask looked pleased.

Of course.

Maro had found depot cook.

"Soup."

"Good?"

"Hot."

Different question.

We ate.

After supper Enna finished day sheets.

She checked my ledger.

Slowly.

Too slowly.

"You felt vibration through crutch?"

"Yes."

"Good."

Another page.

Then closed.

"Five copper."

There.

First full field day.

Master ledger carried most day.

Earned.

I counted after.

Forty-eight.

Not silver.

Closer.

Money wanted become leg.

Road wanted become road.

Both could be true.

Jorren had taught me.

"Tomorrow," Enna said, "shoulder opening at first light. Crib crew coming from depot. Halen wants exposed subgrade before deciding whether class eight can resume."

"Fuel reserve?"

"Depot steward says one and three-quarter days at normal burn."

Less.

"Weather?"

"Rain after midday."

Of course.

"Contract day two?"

"Yes."

"Master?"

She tapped ledger.

"Unless you become stupid overnight."

"I'll try not."

"Don't try creatively."

Fair.

I went Reed Lamp after.

Trial limb still wrapped.

Evening allowance unused.

Could use thirty minutes.

Stable depot lanes.

Skin good.

Time available.

I wanted to.

That mattered.

I also had tired hip from morning wear, full field day, wagon, crutches, standing.

Not pain.

Just tired.

Baseline brain started calculating.

Thirty minutes tonight might produce useful data.

Or fatigue noise.

Tomorrow field day mattered more.

Masta's paper said maximum.

Not assignment.

I left shell wrapped.

Wrote:

**Evening wear: not used. General fatigue after field day. No skin concern. Preserve next-day quality.**

That felt annoyingly mature.

Sori saw.

"You didn't wear it."

"No."

"Good."

"Stop approving me."

"No."

Dask had map open.

Merehook circled.

Not by him.

Printed red route ring.

"Apparently Merehook has old tide observatory," he said.

Of course it did.

Maro said, "Salt cliffs."

Sori said, "We have three days contract minimum."

Nobody said after.

Didn't need.

I looked at sign through window.

Road northeast disappeared behind cottages.

Two days.

First plan had been two nights total.

Funny.

I counted money once.

Forty-eight copper.

Twenty-three Vale.

Bits unknown.

Trial leg still not mine.

Causeway still not solved.

Fuel still south.

Rain coming.

Good day.

Complicated.

# CHAPTER 430

## THE RECORDER

Rain made good clock.

Nothing like weather to make professionals stop pretending time abstract.

First light at Section Three.

Crib crew already there.

Four workers.

One pry bar long enough to become family heirloom.

Enna had no coffee.

Good hierarchy.

Crutches only.

Morning skin fine.

Baseline brain approved.

Annoying.

Not catastrophic.

Worse.

Timber transverse to road.

Stone fill between.

Not fully broken.

Split enough.

"There."

"Yes."

"Toll Venn."

Another Venn.

Of course.

No relation unless proven.

I wrote Toll Venn, crib foreman.

Toll tapped split timber with hammer.

Dull.

"Old piece."

"Older than repair stones. Could be original east shoulder."

"Can it carry class eight?"

"Not like this."

Jorren swore.

Tera did not smile.

Good.

"Problem isn't just split. Fill went somewhere."

"Marsh," one worker said.

Toll looked at him.

"Brilliant."

Worker shrugged.

Different sarcasm academy risk.

But foremen allowed some.

Halen asked, "Drain slot?"

Worker crawled lower shoulder on plank.

"Clear mouth."

"Behind?"

"Can't see."

Toll said, "We open another two stones."

Enna nodded.

Traffic stayed held.

Class six village carts had queue south and north.

Not huge.

Enough.

Milk.

School cart.

Clinic supplies.

One old man with chickens.

Chickens hated infrastructure.

Reasonable.

Second stone came out.

Then third.

Pocket wider than first visible.

Not cavern.

Maybe two arm lengths along shoulder.

Fill had slumped toward old drainage seam.

"Can crib."

Jorren immediately: "Today?"

Toll looked at sky.

"Before hard rain, maybe temporary."

"Class ten?"

"No."

"Class eight?"

"Maybe after load test."

There.

Practical engineering language.

Not miracle.

Not answer.

"Two bells to crib. Another half for stone and load spread if materials here."

"Rain?"

"If starts soft, we work. If hard, stop before fill turns soup."

Jorren said, "Fuel convoy can split class seven."

"How?" Enna asked.

"Not all. Some. Transfer from two tank wagons into four smaller road drums and two class-seven flatbeds."

"Maybe third convoy capacity first run."

"Enough for depot?"

Then Enna.

"Yes. Cost."

"Guild eats transfer labor if Works clears class seven temporary. Depot pays normal freight."

She narrowed eyes.

Honest.

Tera nodded.

Not gratitude.

Alignment.

Enna said, "Nothing moves until Toll finishes and Halen recommends."

Jorren looked at sky.

"Rain doesn't care about recommendation."

Halen said, "Road doesn't care about fuel."

"People do."

"Then perhaps people should maintain roads before fuel sits on them."

There.

That one landed poorly.

Tera turned.

"Perhaps city should fund roads before village tax gets sent south."

Halen stopped.

Enna looked at him.

He rubbed forehead.

"That was not my jurisdiction."

Good.

Human.

Not relevant.

Different orientation.

Soft.

Fine mist.

"We keep."

"That sounds boring."

By second bell cribbing in.

Temporary.

Visible.

Not pretty.

At repaired shoulder:

No grind.

Growth.

Halen recommendation:

Temporary class-seven restricted passage possible at Section Three under spotter.

One wagon at time.

Walking pace.

No stopping on repair.

Inspect shoulder after every third class-seven heavy pass and after any audible grind or visible movement.

Suspend immediately if rain becomes hard or water rises into exposed repair zone.

"Continue transfer."

"Of course."

Not hard.

Yet.

North Reach behind us now.

Fuel beyond south.

Road problem in middle.

Section Two smelled like wet timber.

Dull member under culvert approach easier access than Section Three because shoulder lower.

"Rot pocket."

"Extent?"

"One member maybe adjacent end. Need probe."

Toll pushed.

Wood accepted too much.

"There."

"Yes."

"Today?"

"If you stop asking today, maybe today."

Good.

One worker stood knee-deep clearing wrack from upstream side.

Not me.

Obviously.

One finger over twenty minutes.

Then two.

Not panic.

Sharp.

"Move!"

Not flood wall.

Fast brown push.

His boot slipped.

One leg dropped off edge into channel.

Toll grabbed harness strap.

Other worker grabbed Toll.

Chain.

I was ten paces away.

Crutches.

Old locked-in part noticed geometry instantly.

Do not run.

No need.

I planted right crutch, swung left side forward, got to dry anchor post two paces faster than careful walking.

Worker's loose tool bag sliding toward channel.

Not person.

Tool bag.

I caught strap with crutch tip and hooked it against stone.

Useful.

Not heroic.

Toll and other worker hauled man back.

Nobody injured except dignity.

Water blasted through cleared culvert.

Level dropped almost immediately.

Enna looked at me.

"You good?"

"Yes."

Worker on plank coughed.

"I'm good."

Toll said, "You owe channel apology."

"Fuck channel."

I recorded event:

Wrack release.

Sudden increased culvert flow.

Worker footing loss during withdrawal.

Recovered by harness assistance.

No injury reported.

Tool bag caught before water entry.

No heroics from me.

Good.

Water level on upstream stake fell more than three fingers in ten minutes after blockage cleared.

"Learning."

"Hate it."

Rot timber still real.

Multiple truths again.

Fourth bell nearing.

"Hard band by fifth."

Test seven here or no fuel today.

"Ready enough for one."

Spotters.

Expensive.

Slow.

Not answer.

Obviously.

roughly **2.4 days**.

Mostly.

Not verdict.
